hooks.command: if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then flock -n /tmp/code-review-graph.lock code-review-graph update --skip-flows; rc=$?; [ "$rc" = 1 ] && exit 0; exit $rc; else code-review-graph update --skip-flows; fi

_comment: Personal global Claude Code config. Canonical project baseline lives at workflows/templates/CLAUDE_SETTINGS_TEMPLATE.json in dev-tools. When you add a permission, update the matching _notes group so the rationale stays explicit — grep shows what, _notes shows why.

allow.awk_classification: awk classification probes — added 2026-05-04 mission 2026-05-04-2 (downstream of 2026-05-04-1 harness-pilot-redirect-to-dev-tools which surfaced 4 user-visible awk approval prompts during Reviewer + Analyst dispatches). Both bare `Bash(awk *)` and absolute-path `Bash(/usr/bin/awk *)` forms needed: specialists may invoke `/usr/bin/awk` explicitly to avoid asdf-managed shim resolution per memory feedback_pre_auth_scan_at_triage.md class 17. Spaced form (`awk *`) per word-boundary precedent from mission 2026-05-03-3 (avoids matching `awkward` etc.). Bounded by 4 deny entries against pipe-to-shell shapes (`Bash(awk * | sh)`, `Bash(awk * | bash)`, etc.). Residual risks (two — accept as known limitations per Shell Safety review): (a) `system("...")` calls inside awk programs are unbounded by prefix matchers (string-internal, can't pattern-match); (b) indirection via xargs (`awk '...' | xargs sh -c {}`, `awk '...' | xargs -I{} bash -c {}`) escapes the pipe-to-shell deny because xargs is the executor, not a shell pipe target. Cross-link: memory precedent block 2026-05-04 in feedback_pre_auth_scan_at_triage.md (probe-shape catalog by dispatch role); HANDOFF pending `pipe-to-shell-deny-coverage-zsh-dash-fish-csh` (cross-shell coverage gap across awk + curl + wget — separate mission).
allow.builtins: Core Claude Code tools used on every turn. Always on.
allow.git_read: Read-only git ops — status/diff/log/show/branch/fetch/remote/config/submodule/rev-parse/stash. Safe anywhere; deny list gates the destructive counterparts.
allow.git_write: Low-risk write ops — checkout, switch, add, commit, mv, and reset --soft (never --hard; that's in deny). Push is scoped to feature/ wip/ fix/ chore/ refactor/ branches; main/master push falls through to ask. Rebase is scoped to origin/main|master so the agent can't rewrite arbitrary history during a rebase-onto.
allow.gh: GitHub CLI read-ish ops — pr/issue/run/api/repo. Reviewers dispatched via /review-pr rely on these.
allow.fs_shell: Shell utilities used to move text and inspect files — ls, cat, head, tail, wc, which, find, grep, rg, sort, uniq, diff, echo, pwd, date. Includes benign writes (mkdir, chmod +x, touch, xargs) and compression utilities (gunzip, gzip, tar). Filesystem traversal (cp/mv/ln/rm) lives in `fs_traversal` below — moved out of `fs_shell` 2026-05-03 (mission 2026-05-03-3) when the rm-stays-in-ask claim was inverted. Added 2026-05-01 (mission 2026-05-01-6): gunzip/gzip/tar to support research-workflow decompression (e.g., wayback `id_` route returning gzipped HTML); root-cause Bash-redirect-into-crew-tmp-flagged-as-sensitive issue tracked separately as a Workflow Improvement TODO.
allow.fs_traversal: Filesystem-traversal verbs — cp, mv, ln, rm — pre-authorized as bare allow entries (`Bash(cp *)`, `Bash(mv *)`, `Bash(ln *)`, `Bash(rm *)`). Closes pre-auth-scan class 8 (memory `feedback_pre_auth_scan_at_triage.md`). **Safety boundary:** Claude Code permission precedence is `deny > ask > allow, first match wins` (verified 2026-05-03 mission 2026-05-03-3 by Shell Safety Reviewer against https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions); the existing `rm -rf` deny entries (`rm -rf /`, `rm -rf /*`, `rm -rf ~`, `rm -rf ~/*`, `rm -rf .`) and ask entries (`Bash(rm -rf *)`, `Bash(rm -r *)`) take precedence over the new `Bash(rm *)` allow, so destructive recursive forms still hit deny/ask. Non-recursive `rm` forms (single-file `rm <path>`, multi-file `rm a b c`, force-but-non-recursive `rm -f <path>`) are the only things this allow unlocks; any `-r` / `-rf` form falls through to ask or deny. **Trailing space convention:** all four entries use `Bash(<verb> *)` (with space) so the matcher requires a word boundary — prevents accidental matches against future `cpio`-style binaries. **Known tradeoffs:** (a) `ln -sf <evil> ~/.claude/<file>` could clobber via symlink (rare; PreToolUse cross-project warning hook adds advisory coverage), (b) `mv` is destructive on the source side and crosses project boundaries silently (covered by same PreToolUse hook). Cross-link: HANDOFF mission `bash-allow-list-expansion-filesystem-and-version-managers` (this mission), HANDOFF pending `pretooluse-bash-matcher-outcome-logging-hook` (Layer-2 friction observability).
allow.humio_search_script: Allows direct invocation of ~/.claude/skills/humio-search/scripts/humio_search.py without per-call approval prompts; sub-agents (Investigator/Analyst/Reviewer) routinely query Humio for log evidence at Phase 0 and during root-cause investigation. Both tilde and absolute-path forms required per memory class 17 (absolute-path-binary defeats command-name prefix matchers). Read-only HTTP queries to Humio (cloud.humio.com via HUMIO_BASE_URL env). humio_search.py source audit (mission 2026-05-04-4 Shell Safety Reviewer briefing): pure urllib.request + argparse + json — no subprocess/os.system/shell=True/exec/eval, no filesystem writes, no path-traversal. Pipe-to-shell residual exec risk: existing curl/wget/awk-shape pipe-to-shell deny entries match by command-prefix (curl/wget/awk), so they do NOT intercept `humio_search.py * | sh`/`| bash`; the actual safety net is fall-through to user-approval ask-tier. If a future incident motivates structural intercept, add parallel `Bash(*humio_search.py* | sh*)` / `| bash*` / cross-shell denies (HANDOFF pending `pipe-to-shell-deny-coverage-zsh-dash-fish-csh` covers the cross-shell sibling). Residual risk 1 (LLM-input-trust, NOT shell-safety): Humio log content returned to agent as JSON; attackers who can plant data in Humio (log-forging) may inject instructions the agent might act on; this allow envelope does NOT cover content trust. Residual risk 2 (auth-token argv leak): --token <value> lands in ps/shell-history; prefer HUMIO_API_TOKEN env var. Closes HANDOFF pending humio-search-script-allow-entry.
allow.lang: Language runtime probes — python3 for JSON tooling, ruby -v and gem list for Portal/Pricing, cd for shell housekeeping.
allow.uv: Substrate-pilot mission 2026-05-02-11 added uv for pyoxigraph venv install; broad-allow because uv is the canonical modern Python package manager and the asdf-shimmed python3 resolves to 3.6.15 (too old for pyoxigraph) while Homebrew's python3.13 rejects pip install --user per PEP 668. uv venv + uv pip install is the clean isolation path.
allow.version_managers: Language version managers — asdf, pyenv, nvm, rbenv — pre-authorized as bare allow entries (`Bash(asdf *)`, `Bash(pyenv *)`, `Bash(nvm *)`, `Bash(rbenv *)`). Closes pre-auth-scan class 9 (memory `feedback_pre_auth_scan_at_triage.md`) — common during cross-stack work for runtime version detection (e.g., `asdf list python` to choose `namedtuple` vs `@dataclass` for compat; `nvm current` for Node-script compatibility). **Safety boundary:** `<vm> install` operations download + compile arbitrary upstream code — same trust class as `brew install` — and are gated in `ask` (see `_notes.ask.version_manager_writes`). Read-only inspection (`asdf list`, `pyenv versions`, `nvm current`, `rbenv which`) and local-state changes (`asdf reshim`, `pyenv rehash`, `asdf global/local`) remain broadly allowed because they don't fetch network code. Cross-link: HANDOFF mission `bash-allow-list-expansion-filesystem-and-version-managers` (this mission); brew precedent in `ask.system_mgmt`.
allow.build_fetch: Build and fetch — make, npx, npm, curl -s (silent), curl -fsS (silent + fail-on-HTTP-error + show-errors), curl -fsSL (same + follow-redirects). Interactive curl falls through; curl|bash and curl|sh are denied. Robust shapes added 2026-05-01 (mission 2026-05-01-6) for the wayback `id_` route research pattern (HANDOFF pending `wayback-id-fetch-pattern`).
allow.docker_read: Read-only docker ops — compose ps, ps, inspect, logs. Mutating ops (run/exec/up/down/restart/build) stay in ask.
allow.dev_tools_scripts: Crew-workflow scripts under ~/Decisiv/dev-tools/scripts/ plus install.sh. Both tilde and absolute paths listed because matchers don't expand ~.
allow.bash_validation: Syntax/lint tools invoked during Shell Safety Reviewer pre-flight — bash -n and shellcheck.
allow.skills: Personal skill invocations that don't need per-run confirmation — oauth, srm-gateway, update-config.
allow.mcp_read: Read-only MCP operations — Atlassian (Jira/Confluence fetch, search, metadata), CircleCI (pipeline status, logs, test results), code-review-graph (all), Slack (read/search). Write counterparts (create/edit/transition/post) stay in ask.
allow.web_fetch: WebFetch pre-approved domains — GitHub (github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com) for PR context; Anthropic surface (code.claude.com, docs.claude.com, platform.claude.com, anthropic.com, www.anthropic.com, claude.ai, console.anthropic.com, support.anthropic.com, help.claude.com, status.claude.com, status.anthropic.com) for model/API research, account/console, support, and incident-status. WebFetch's redirect-following requires per-host allowlisting and the matcher grammar does not support wildcards (no `*.claude.com`), so each subdomain is listed explicitly. Wider Anthropic surface added 2026-05-01 (mission S1 — friction-reduction batch, pre-empts per-redirect approval prompts; HANDOFF pending `pre-approve-anthropic-webfetch-surface`). Engine-default prompt-on-no-match is the catch-all for everything else (no explicit ask[WebFetch] needed — bare ask rule was removed 2026-05-06 per /doctor unreachable-rules diagnosis; it was shadowing all 27 specific allows). WebSearch is always on. **Track-A-bounded** (added 2026-04-30, mission 2026-04-30-8 — remove when eval/framework cluster Track A surveys complete + Track D synthesis lands; tracked in HANDOFF.md pending `track-a-webfetch-cleanup`): docs.crewai.com, microsoft.github.io, langchain-ai.github.io, mastra.ai, learn.microsoft.com. **Substrate-tool-family-bounded** (added 2026-05-02, mission 2026-05-02-9 — pre-empts per-domain approval prompts during composition #4 graph-DB / RDF / search-index / relational-as-graph candidate surveys; remove when downstream pilot mission lands and tool family is selected; tracked in HANDOFF.md pending `substrate-tool-family-webfetch-cleanup`): kuzudb.github.io, kuzudb.com, oxigraph.org, networkx.org, sqlite.org, duckdb.org, www.w3.org, docs.rs, cozodb.org. **GitHub repo content goes through `gh` CLI**, not WebFetch — github.com WebFetch is only for PR pages, README rendering, and similar HTML; raw repo file content uses `gh api ... -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github.v3.raw'` per memory `feedback_github_repo_inspection.md`.
allow.fs_scopes: Explicit Read/Edit/Write scopes — full access under ~/Decisiv/ and /private/tmp/, and ~/.claude/crew-tmp/ (crew-scratch; also listed in additionalDirectories so subprocesses can write here without prompting).
allow.matcher_quirks: Two Bash matchers that exist only to work around matcher-expansion corner cases — Bash(git init:*) covers the colon-prefixed invocation pattern that bare Bash(git *) wouldn't match, and Bash(/bin/ls:*) handles a PATH-resolved ls callsite the bare Bash(ls*) matcher misses.

deny.destructive_bash: Filesystem wipeout — rm -rf /, ~, ., *; mkfs; dd to /dev/*; chmod 777. Hard-blocked because the recovery cost is too high for an agent turn to own.
deny.privilege_escalation: sudo, su, doas, pkexec — any ask for elevated privileges should come from the human, not the agent.
deny.force_push: --no-verify (skips hooks), --force / -f, push origin +* — rewriting shared history bypasses the human checkpoint; keep it gated at the deny layer.
deny.destructive_git: reset --hard, clean -fdx, checkout -- ., branch -D main|master — all destroy local work or protected refs.
deny.destructive_docker: volume rm/prune, system prune, rm -f, stop/kill — losing a container's state is hard to undo and Portal/Pricing share the porcing volume.
deny.curl_pipe_shell: curl|bash, curl|sh, wget|bash, wget|sh — the canonical supply-chain footgun.
deny.secrets: Read/Grep against ~/.ssh/, *.gpg/*.asc, AWS SSO + CLI caches, accessKeys.csv, .netrc, docker config.json, .vault-token. These must never be shown to a model.

ask.destructive_confirmable: rm -rf * / rm -r * — destructive but sometimes legitimate (scratch cleanup). Human gates each instance.
ask.env_introspection: env, printenv — may surface secrets from shell env; ask before dumping.
ask.system_mgmt: launchctl, brew, kill -9, pkill — scheduled tasks and global software state; confirm before mutating.
ask.version_manager_writes: Network-fetching + compile operations on language version managers — `asdf install`, `asdf plugin add`, `asdf plugin update`, `pyenv install`, `nvm install`, `rbenv install`. Mirrors the `brew *` ask gate (same trust class: download + compile arbitrary upstream code; `asdf plugin add <name> <url>` clones an arbitrary git repo, `asdf plugin update` git-pulls from potentially-modified upstream). Local-state version-manager ops (list, current, which, reshim, global, local, plugin remove) stay in allow (see `_notes.allow.version_managers`). Added 2026-05-03 (mission 2026-05-03-3) per Shell Safety Reviewer's brew-inconsistency finding; `plugin add` / `plugin update` added same mission per Shell Safety Reviewer's diff-review Warning W1.
ask.docker_mutating: docker run/exec/compose up/down/restart/build — start/stop services. Read counterparts are in allow.docker_read.
ask.postgres: pg_dump, pg_restore, psql — DB interactions against porcing; gate each one.
ask.main_branch_push: git push origin main|master — pushing to protected branches always needs a human checkpoint.
ask.mcp_writes: Atlassian create/edit/transition/comment, Slack send/schedule, CircleCI run_pipeline/rerun — outbound actions that change shared state.
ask.env_files: Read/Grep against **/.env*, credentials*, *secret*, *.token, *password*, *.pem, *.key — possible secret exposure; confirm case by case.
ask.shell_profiles: Read/Write/Edit against ~/.bashrc, ~/.bash_profile, ~/.zshrc, ~/.zshenv, ~/.zprofile — shell startup files; any change affects every future terminal session.

hooks.PostToolUse: After Edit/Write/Bash, update the code-review-graph incrementally. Flock-guarded and non-blocking.
hooks.SessionStart: Two hooks: (1) code-review-graph status summary; (2) dev-tools check-handoff warns on stale HANDOFF.md.
hooks.Stop: At turn end, code-review-graph detect-changes --brief surfaces risk-scored structural impact.
hooks.UserPromptSubmit: Enforces MISSION_LOG.md initialization on prompts with execution intent — fires only when the working dir lacks a mission log and the prompt contains an intent keyword.
hooks.SubagentStop: Logs sub-agent completion to MISSION_LOG.md — one `Dispatch of <Role> completed` line per finish.
hooks.PreToolUse: Before Bash/Edit/Write, warn if the command or target path reaches into another Decisiv repo. Advisory (exit 0), skips safe-prefix commands and data-only path mentions.

_notes.skillListingBudgetFraction: Fraction of context window reserved for the skill listing sent to Claude. Schema (per v2.1.131 binary, `claude-code` Zod): `number().gt(0).lte(1).optional()`, default 0.01 = 1%. Raised to 0.02 (2%) on 2026-05-06 (mission 2026-05-06) after `/doctor` reported 1.3% utilization → 7 skill descriptions truncated (named: prep, hooks, address-reviews, +4 more). Disable-skills path was investigated but rejected — JSONL grep underestimated invocation counts for several mission-flow-critical skills (e.g., /crew-stats and /validate-artifacts run at every mission close, but the user-visible invocation channel apparently doesn't surface in session JSONL grepping that I performed). 0.02 ≈ 50% headroom over observed 1.3% need. The env var `SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET` is an absolute-character override that takes precedence over this fraction when set; we use the fraction so the budget scales with context-window growth. Public docs (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills) only document the env var as of 2026-05-06; the fraction key is binary-resident but undocumented — confirm with `/doctor` after each Claude Code upgrade in case the schema changes.
